articles.diffFindings: No file that renders, validates or runs the E-signature Settings page, the signing connector API, the webhook route, reconciliation, executed-copy filing or the Envelope send route changed. settings.tsx adds a Return to setup link that shows only when an Administrator arrives from the setup wizard; the rail, the Integrations entry and the role gate are unchanged. list-editor.tsx gains optional collapsible props; settings-e-signature.tsx does not use ListEditor. The sign-in page now shows organization branding; the Email, Password and Sign in controls are unchanged. The AI connector refactor and the new intro text belong to configure-analysis. d64309f5 rewords BASE_URL as browser-facing and allows a private origin, but changes no app code. The article already says a blank Public callback URL uses the app address, which must then be publicly reachable for Webhook, so it stays correct. No message id used by the E-signature pane changed.

steps.action: Open Settings > Organization > Integrations > E-signature; check the unconfigured card
Expand DocuSign; check default controls in Polling mode
Select Save connector with every field blank (Polling)
Choose Webhook; check the extra fields and the missing-HMAC refusal
Webhook: enter a non-HTTPS Public callback URL and save
API refusals for incomplete saves (authenticated requests, no browser navigation)
Save a fictional connector in Polling mode; reload; check the saved state
Test connection with the unreadable fictional key
Change the saved Polling connector to Webhook without an HMAC secret, then with one
Webhook mode: post an unsigned and a signed fictional delivery for an unknown Envelope
Switch back to Polling; check the Webhook fields leave and a signed delivery is refused
Turn off Send for signature from records; test; save a change while off
Turn the connector back on, then remove it
Open the E-signature Settings page as a Legal Team Member
